decisions.reason: This software is very close to the firm's automation, digital support, and data-driven infrastructure capabilities, and its own webpage suggests sufficient commitment to keep learning and improve it commercially.

It also fits the firm's software and process-data knowledge base, but because it was only mentioned rather than prominently presented, management would keep it with more caution while assessing differentiation and uptake.

The product draws on the firm's engineering and infrastructure project experience, yet it is less central to the firm's move toward connected and data-driven systems, so it is kept but with a higher review risk.

A floating sludge extractor is closely related to the firm's machinery and water-infrastructure application knowledge, giving it good scope to refine the product through existing engineering capabilities.

Control technology for water engineering machinery sits at the core of the firm's absorptive capacity in automation, interoperable systems, and operational services, so management would strongly favor retaining it.
